questions.q: The remainder on dividing ${5}^{99}$ by $11$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
Now to divide ${5}^{99}$ by $11$ we need to check the cyclicity of power of $5$ when divided by $11$,

So remainder when $\dfrac{{5}^{1}}{11} \to 5\text{as remainder}$

Similarly,

$\dfrac{{5}^{2}}{11} = \dfrac{25}{11} \to 3\text{as remainder}$

$\dfrac{{5}^{3}}{11} = \dfrac{125}{11} \to 4\text{as remainder}$

$\dfrac{{5}^{4}}{11} = \dfrac{625}{11} \to 9\text{as remainder}$

And $\dfrac{{5}^{5}}{11} = \dfrac{3125}{11} \to 1\text{as remainder}$

So, rewriting the expression we get, ${\left({5}^{5}\right)}^{19} \times {5}^{4}$

Now when $\dfrac{{\left({5}^{5}\right)}^{19} \times {5}^{4}}{11} \to 1 \times \dfrac{{5}^{4}}{11}$

Now again simplifying we get, $\dfrac{{5}^{4}}{11} \to 9\text{as remainder}$.

questions.q: The remainder, when ${7}^{103}$ is divided by $17,$ is
questions.solution:
Using the binomial expansion in ${7}^{103} = {\left({7}^{2}\right)}^{51} \cdot 7 = {\left(51 - 2\right)}^{51} \cdot 7$ we get,

${\left(51 - 2\right)}^{51} \cdot 7 = 7 \cdot \left(C0 51 {51}^{51} \cdot {2}^{0} - C1 51 {51}^{50} \cdot {2}^{1} + . . . . . . . - C51 51 {2}^{51}\right)$

Now $51$ is divisible by $17$, so when above equation is divided by $17$ we get, $7 \cdot \left(- {2}^{51}\right)$ as remainder,

Now again using binomial in $7 \cdot \left(- {2}^{51}\right) = - 56{\left({2}^{4}\right)}^{12} = - 56{\left(17 - 1\right)}^{12}$ we get,

$- 56{\left(17 - 1\right)}^{12} = - 56\left(C0 12 {17}^{12} \cdot {1}^{0} - C1 12 {17}^{11} \cdot {1}^{1} + . . . . . . . + C12 12 {1}^{12}\right)$

Now dividing above equation by $17$ we get,

$\left(- 56 \times 1\right) \div 17 = - 5$,

Now changing negative remainder to positive we get, $- 5 + 17 = 12$,

Hence, when ${7}^{103}$ divided by $17$ gives $12$ as remainder.

questions.q: The number of elements in the set ${ n \in { 1, 2, 3, \ldots , 100 } ∣ \left( 11{)}^{n} > ( 10{)}^{n} + ( 9{)}^{n}\right\}$ is ___________.
questions.solution:
We have to check ${11}^{n} > {10}^{n} + {9}^{n}$

$⇒ {11}^{n} - {9}^{n} > {10}^{n}$

$⇒ ( 10 + 1{)}^{n} - ( 10 - 1{)}^{n} > {10}^{n}$

Using ${\left(a + b\right)}^{n} - {\left(a - b\right)}^{n} = 2\left[C1 n \cdot {a}^{n - 1} \cdot b + C3 n \cdot {a}^{n - 3} \cdot {b}^{3} + C5 n \cdot {a}^{n - 5} \cdot {b}^{5} + . . .\right]$

$⇒ 2\left[C1 n \cdot {10}^{n - 1} + C3 n \cdot {10}^{n - 3} + C5 n \cdot {10}^{n - 5} + ⋯ ⋯\right] > {10}^{n}$

$⇒ 2n \cdot {10}^{n - 1} + 2\left[C3 n \cdot {10}^{n - 3} + C5 n \cdot {10}^{n - 5} + ⋯ ⋯\right] > {10}^{n}$ $\ldots \left(1\right)$

For $n = 5,$ the $L . H . S .$ is $2 \cdot 5 \cdot {10}^{4} + 2\left[C3 5 \cdot {10}^{2} + C5 5\right]$

$⇒ {10}^{5} + 2\left[C3 5 \cdot {10}^{2} + C5 5\right] > {10}^{5}$ which is true.

Now, for $n = 6, 7, 8, \ldots \ldots , 100$

$2n \cdot {10}^{n - 1} > {10}^{n}$

$⇒ 2n \cdot {10}^{n - 1} + 2\left[C3 n \cdot {10}^{n - 3} + C5 n \cdot {10}^{n - 5} + ⋯ ⋯\right] > {10}^{n}$

$⇒ {11}^{n} - {9}^{n} > {10}^{n}$ for all $n = 5, 6, 7, \ldots \ldots , 100$

For $n = 4,$ the inequality $\left(1\right)$ is not satisfied.

Hence, the inequality does not hold good for $n = 1, 2, 3, 4$

So, required number of elements$= 96 .$

questions.q: Let $z$ and $w$ be two complex numbers such that $w = z\overset{¯}{z} - 2z + 2, \left|\dfrac{z + i}{z - 3i}\right| = 1$ and $Re \left(w\right)$ has minimum value. Then, the minimum value of $n \in N$ for which ${w}^{n}$ is real, is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
$\omega = z\overset{¯}{z} - 2z + 2$

$\left|\dfrac{z + i}{z - 3i}\right| = 1$

$⇒ \left|z + i\right| = \left|z - 3i\right|$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {\left(y + 1\right)}^{2} = {x}^{2} + {\left(y - 3\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ y = 1$

$⇒ z = x + i, x \in R$

$\omega = \left(x + i\right)\left(x - i\right) - 2\left(x + i\right) + 2$

$= {x}^{2} + 1 - 2x - 2i + 2$

$Re \left(\omega\right) = {x}^{2} - 2x + 3 = {\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + 2$

For min $\left(Re\left(\omega\right)\right), x = 1$

$⇒ \omega = 2 - 2i = 2\left(1 - i\right) = 2\sqrt{2}{e}^{- i\dfrac{\pi}{4}}$

${\omega}^{n} = {\left(2\sqrt{2}\right)}^{n}{e}^{- i\dfrac{n\pi}{4}}$

For real and minimum value of $n$,

$n = 4$

questions.q: Let $S =${$z \in \mathbb{C}: \left|z - 3\right| \le 1$ and$z\left(4 + 3i\right) + \overset{¯}{z}\left(4 - 3i\right) \le 24$}. If $\alpha + i\beta$ is the point in $S$ which is closest to $4i$, then $25\left(\alpha + \beta\right)$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left|z - 3\right| \le 1$

Which represent a circle of radius $1$ and centred at $\left(3, 0\right)$

Now simplifying $z\left(4 + 3i\right) + \overset{¯}{z}\left(4 - 3i\right) \le 24$

We get, $\left(x + iy\right)\left(4 + 3i\right) + \left(x - iy\right)\left(4 - 3i\right) \le 24$

$⇒ 4x + 3xi + 4iy - 3y + 4x - 3ix - 4iy - 3y \le 24$

$⇒ 8x - 6y \le 24$

$⇒ 4x - 3y \le 12$

Now plotting the diagram we get,

Minimum distance of $\left(0, 4\right)$ from circle $= \sqrt{{3}^{2} + {4}^{2}} - 1 = 4$ will lie along line joining $\left(0, 4\right) \text{ and } \left(3, 0\right)$
$∴$ equation line
$\dfrac{x}{3} + \dfrac{y}{4} = 1 ⇒ 4x + 3y = 12 \ldots \left(i\right)$
Equation of circle ${\left(x - 3\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1 \ldots \left(ii\right)$

Solving (i) and (ii) we get,

${\left(\dfrac{12 - 3y}{4} - 3\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1$

${\left(\dfrac{- 3y}{4}\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1$

$\dfrac{25{y}^{2}}{16} = 1 ⇒ y = \pm \dfrac{4}{5}$

So, for minimum distance $y = \dfrac{4}{5}$

$∴ x = \dfrac{12}{5}$

$∴ 25\left(\alpha + \beta\right) = 25\left(\dfrac{4}{5} + \dfrac{12}{5}\right)$

$⇒ 16 \times 5 = 80$

questions.q: Let $z = a + ib, b \ne 0$ be complex numbers satisfying ${z}^{2} = \overset{¯}{z} \cdot {2}^{1 - \left|z\right|}$. Then the least value of $n \in N$, such that ${z}^{n} = {\left(z + 1\right)}^{n}$, is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Given,

${z}^{2} = \overset{¯}{z} \cdot {2}^{1 - \left|z\right|} ⋯ \left(1\right)$

On taking modulus both side we get,

$⇒ {\left|z\right|}^{2} = \left|z\right| \cdot {2}^{1 - \left|z\right|}$

$⇒ \left|z\right| = {2}^{1 - \left|z\right|}, ∵ b \ne 0 ⇒ \left|z\right| \ne 0$

So comparing both side we get $\left|z\right| = 1 ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Now putting $z = a + ib$ then $\sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}} = 1 ⋯ \left(3\right)$

Now again from equation $\left(1\right)$, equation $\left(2\right)$, equation $\left(3\right)$ we get:

${a}^{2} - {b}^{2} + i2ab = \left(a - ib\right){2}^{0} = a - ib$

Now on comaparing imagenary and real part we get,

$∴ {a}^{2} - {b}^{2} = a$ and $2ab = - b$

Now solving we get, $a = - \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $b = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

So, $z = - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$ or $= - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$

Now solving ${z}^{n} = {\left(z + 1\right)}^{n} ⇒ {\left(\dfrac{z + 1}{z}\right)}^{n} = 1$

$⇒ {\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{z}\right)}^{n} = 1$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{3}i}{2}\right)}^{n} = 1$

$⇒ {\left(- {\omega}^{2}\right)}^{n} = 1$, then minimum value of $n$ is $6$

questions.q: Sum of squares of modulus of all the complex numbers $z$ satisfying $\overset{¯}{z} = i{z}^{2} + {z}^{2} - z$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$z + \overset{¯}{z} = {izz}^{2} + {z}^{2}$

Consider $z = x + iy$

$2x = \left(i + 1\right)\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2xyi\right)$

On comparing real and imaginary part we get,

$⇒ 2x = {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} - 2xy$ and ${x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2xy = 0$

$⇒ 2x = - 4xy$

$⇒ x = 0$ or $y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

Case 1: $x = 0 ⇒ 2 \times 0 = \left(i + 1\right)\left({0}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2 \times 0 \times yi\right)y = 0$

Here $z = 0$

Case 2: $y = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$⇒ 4{x}^{2} - 4x - 1 = 0$

${\left(2x - 1\right)}^{2} = 2$

$2x - 1 = \pm \sqrt{2}$

$x = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{2}}{2}$

Here $z = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{i}{2}$ or $z = \dfrac{1 - \sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{i}{2}$

Sum of squares of modulus of $z$

$= 0 + \dfrac{{\left(1 + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{2} + 1}{4} + \dfrac{{\left(1 - \sqrt{2}\right)}^{2} + 1}{4} = \dfrac{8}{4} = 2$

questions.q: Let $a, b, c, d$ be in arithmetic progression with common difference $\lambda$. If $\left|\begin{cases}x + a - c & x + b & x + a \\ x - 1 & x + c & x + b \\ x - b + d & x + d & x + c\end{cases}\right| = 2$, then value of ${\lambda}^{2}$ is equal to________.
questions.solution:
Since, $a, b, c \text{ and } d$ are in $A . P .$, therefore

$b - a = c - b = d - c = \lambda$

We have,

$\left|\begin{cases}x + a - c & x + b & x + a \\ x - 1 & x + c & x + b \\ x - b + d & x + d & x + c\end{cases}\right| = 2$

${C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} - {C}_{3}$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}x - 2\lambda & \lambda & x + a \\ x - 1 & \lambda & x + b \\ x + 2\lambda & \lambda & x + c\end{cases}\right| = 2$

${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} - {R}_{1}, {R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - {R}_{1}$

$\left|\begin{cases}x - 2\lambda & \lambda & x + a \\ 2\lambda - 1 & 0 & b - a \\ 4\lambda & 0 & c - a\end{cases}\right| = 2$

$⇒ \lambda\left|\begin{cases}x - 2\lambda & 1 & x + a \\ 2\lambda - 1 & 0 & \lambda \\ 4\lambda & 0 & 2\lambda\end{cases}\right| = 2$

$⇒ - \lambda\left(4{\lambda}^{2} - 4{\lambda}^{2} - 2\lambda\right) = 2$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{D}_{k} = \left|\begin{cases}n & n\left(n + 1\right) & {n}^{2} \\ n & {n}^{2} + n + 2 & {n}^{2} \\ n & {n}^{2} + n & {n}^{2} + n + 2\end{cases}\right|$

${R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} - {R}_{2}$ and ${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} - {R}_{3}$

questions.q: Let $A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & a & a \\ 0 & 1 & b \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right], a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. If for some $n \in N, {A}^{n} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 48 & 2160 \\ 0 & 1 & 96 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$ then $n + a + b$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & a & a \\ 0 & 1 & b \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

Now on rearranging we get,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}0 & a & a \\ 0 & 0 & b \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{cases}\right] = I + B$

Now finding ${B}^{2} = \left[\begin{cases}0 & a & a \\ 0 & 0 & b \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}0 & a & a \\ 0 & 0 & b \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}0 & 0 & ab \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{cases}\right]$

And ${B}^{3} = 0$

Now by using binomial expansion we get,${A}^{n} = {\left(1 + B\right)}^{n} = C0 n I + C1 n B + C2 n {B}^{2} + C3 n {B}^{3} + . . .$

$= \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}0 & na & na \\ 0 & 0 & nb \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}0 & 0 & \dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)ab}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{cases}\right]$

$\left(\text{as}{B}^{3}\text{and higher power will become zero}\right)$

$= \left[\begin{cases}1 & na & na + \dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)}{2}ab \\ 0 & 1 & nb \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 48 & 2160 \\ 0 & 1 & 96 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

On comparing we get $na = 48, nb = 96$ and $na + \dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)}{2}ab = 2160$

On solving above equations we get,

$⇒ a = 4, n = 12$ and $b = 8$

So, $n + a + b = 4 + 12 + 8 = 24$

questions.solution:
Given, $A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$ and $A = {A}^{- 1}$

So, ${A}^{2} = A \cdot {A}^{- 1} = I$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}{a}^{2} + bc & ab + bd \\ ac + cd & bc + {d}^{2}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

On comparing both side we get,

$∴ {a}^{2} + bc = 1 ⋯ \left(1\right)$

$ab + bd = 0 ⋯ \left(2\right)$

$ac + cd = 0 ⋯ \left(3\right)$

$bc + {d}^{2} = 1 ⋯ \left(4\right)$

Now equation $\left(1\right) - \left(4\right)$ gives

${a}^{2} - {d}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(a + d\right) = 0$ or $a - d = 0$

Case-I

$a + d = 0 ⇒ \left(a, d\right) = \left(- 1, 1\right), \left(0, 0\right), \left(1, - 1\right)$

Assuming case $\left(a\right)$$⇒ \left(a, d\right) = \left(- 1, 1\right)$

Now from equation $\left(1\right)$

$1 + bc = 1 ⇒ bc = 0$

When $b = 0, c = 12$ possibilities

When $c = 0, b = 12$ possibilities

But $\left(0, 0\right)$ is repeated

$∴ 2 \times 12 = 24$

So, total case will be $24 - 1$ (repeated) $= 23$ pairs.

case $\left(b\right)$ $⇒ \left(a, d\right) = \left(1, - 1\right) ⇒ bc = 0 \to 23$ pairs

case $\left(c\right) ⇒ \left(a, d\right) = \left(0, 0\right) ⇒ bc = 1$

$⇒ \left(b, c\right) = \left(1, 1\right)$ and $\left(- 1, - 1\right) \to 2$ pairs

Case-II

When $a = d$

from $\left(2\right)$ and $\left(3\right)$

$a \ne 0$ then $b = c = 0$

${a}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ a = \pm 1 = d$

$\left(a, d\right) = \left(1, 1\right), \left(- 1, - 1\right) \to 2$ pairs

$∴$ Total $= 23 + 23 + 2 + 2$

$= 50$ pairs.

we get $⇒ \dfrac{9 !}{6 ! 2 ! 1 !} = 252 . . . \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{9 !}{7 ! 2 !} = 36 . . . \left(iii\right)$

Now adding equation $\left(i\right) + \left(ii\right) + \left(iii\right)$

We get $126 + 252 + 36 = 414$

So total $414$ ways will be there.

questions.q: The total number of two digit numbers $' n '$, such that ${3}^{n} + {7}^{n}$ is a multiple of $10$ , is ___ .
questions.solution:
$∵ {7}^{n} = ( 10 - 3{)}^{n} = 10k + ( - 3{)}^{n}$

${7}^{n} + {3}^{n} = 10k + ( - 3{)}^{n} + {3}^{n}$

$10k + {\left(- 3\right)}^{n} + {\left(3\right)}^{n} = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}10k\text{if n=odd} \\ 10k + 2 . {3}^{n}\text{if n=even}\end{array}\right$

Let $n = 2t; t \in N$

$∴ {3}^{n} = {3}^{2t} = ( 10 - 1{)}^{t}$

$= 10p + ( - 1{)}^{t}$

.$= 10p \pm 1$

$∴$ if $n =$ even then ${7}^{n} + {3}^{n}$ will not be multiply of $10$

So if $n$ is odd then only ${7}^{n} + {3}^{n}$ will be multiply of $10$

$∴ n = 11, 13, 15, \ldots \ldots \ldots . , 99$

$∴$ Number of odd two digit numbers $= 45$

Let $N$ be the four digit number $gcd\left(N, 18\right) = 3$

Hence $N$ is an odd integer which is divisible by $3$ but not by $9$.

$4$ digit odd multiples of $3$

$1005, 1011, \ldots , 9999 \to 1500$

digit odd multiples of $9$

$1017, 1035, \ldots , 9999 \to 500$

Hence number of such $N = 1500 - 500 = 1000$

If $p$ and $r$ are the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} - 8ax + 2a = 0$ and $q$ and $s$ are the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} + 12bx + 6b = 0$, such that $\dfrac{1}{p}, \dfrac{1}{q}, \dfrac{1}{r}, \dfrac{1}{s}$ are in A.P., then ${a}^{- 1} - {b}^{- 1}$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Since $p, r$ are roots of ${x}^{2} - 8ax + 2a = 0$ and

$q, s$ are the roots of ${x}^{2} + 12bx + 6b = 0$

So the equation $2a{x}^{2} - 8ax + 1 = 0$ has roots $\dfrac{1}{p}, \dfrac{1}{r}$ and

$6b{x}^{2} + 12bx + 1 = 0$ has roots $\dfrac{1}{q}, \dfrac{1}{s}$.

Given that $\dfrac{1}{p}, \dfrac{1}{q}, \dfrac{1}{r}, \dfrac{1}{s}$ are in A.P.

Let $\dfrac{1}{p} = \alpha - 3\beta, \dfrac{1}{q} = \alpha - \beta, \dfrac{1}{r} = \alpha + \beta$ and $\dfrac{1}{s} = \alpha + 3\beta$

i.e. $\dfrac{1}{p} + \dfrac{1}{r} = 2\alpha - 2\beta = 4$ and

$\dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{1}{s} = 2\alpha + 2\beta = - 2$

or $\alpha = \dfrac{1}{2}, \beta = - \dfrac{3}{2}$

i.e. $\dfrac{1}{p} = 5, \dfrac{1}{q} = 2, \dfrac{1}{r} = - 1, \dfrac{1}{s} = - 4$

Now

$\dfrac{1}{p} \times \dfrac{1}{r} = \dfrac{1}{2a} = - 5 ⇒ \dfrac{1}{a} = - 10$ and $\dfrac{1}{q} \times \dfrac{1}{s} = \dfrac{1}{6b} = - 8 ⇒ \dfrac{1}{b} = - 48$

Hence, ${a}^{- 1} - {b}^{- 1} = - 10 + 48 = 38$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right)$ be a quadratic polynomial with leading coefficient $1$ such that $f\left(0\right) = p, p \ne 0$, and $f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$. If the equations $f\left(x\right) = 0$ and $fofofof\left(x\right) = 0$ have a common real root, then $f\left(- 3\right)$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Let $f\left(x\right) = \left(x - \alpha\right)\left(x - \beta\right)$

It is given that $f\left(0\right) = p ⇒ \alpha\beta = p$

and $f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{3} ⇒ \left(1 - \alpha\right)\left(1 - \beta\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Now let us assume that $\alpha$ is the common root of $f\left(x\right) = 0$ and $fofofof\left(x\right) = 0$

$fofofof\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ fofofof\left(\alpha\right) = 0$

$⇒ fofof\left(0\right) = 0$

$⇒ fof\left(p\right) = 0$

So, $f\left(p\right)$ is either $\alpha$ or $\beta$.

Now assuming $\left(p - \alpha\right)\left(p - \beta\right) = \alpha$

$⇒ \left(\alpha\beta - \alpha\right)\left(\alpha\beta - \beta\right) = \alpha ⇒ \left(\beta - 1\right)\left(\alpha - 1\right)\beta = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{\beta}{3} = 1$ $\left(\text{as}\left(1 - \alpha\right)\left(1 - \beta\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

So, $\beta = 3$

Now finding $\alpha$ by putting the value of $\beta\text{in}\left(1 - \alpha\right)\left(1 - \beta\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$,

$⇒ \left(1 - \alpha\right)\left(1 - 3\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{7}{6}$

So, $f\left(x\right) = \left(x - \dfrac{7}{6}\right)\left(x - 3\right)$

So, $f\left(- 3\right) = \left(- 3 - \dfrac{7}{6}\right)\left(- 3 - 3\right) = 25$

questions.q: Consider a set of $3n$ numbers having variance $4 .$ In this set, the mean of first $2n$ numbers is $6$ and the mean of the remaining $n$ numbers is $3 .$ A new set is constructed by adding $1$ into each of the first $2n$ numbers, and subtracting $1$ from each of the remaining $n$ numbers. If the variance of the new set is $k,$ then $9k$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Let, the number be ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, . . . , {a}_{2n}, {b}_{1}, {b}_{2}, {b}_{3}, . . . , {b}_{n} .$

Given, the mean of the first $2n$ numbers is $6$ and that of the remaining $n$ numbers is $3,$ then by using the formula for combined mean, we get, the mean of the complete set as $\mu = \dfrac{2n \times 6 + n \times 3}{2n + n} = \dfrac{15n}{3n} = 5 .$

Also, the variance is defined as ${\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {\left({x}_{i}\right)}^{2}}{n} - {\left(\mu\right)}^{2}$

$4 = \dfrac{∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + ∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2}}{3n} - ( 5{)}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + ∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2}}{3n} = 29$

$⇒ ∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + ∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2} = 87n . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, as per the given information, the distribution becomes

${a}_{1} + 1, {a}_{2} + 1, {a}_{3} + 1, . . . , {a}_{2n} + 1, {b}_{1} - 1, {b}_{2} - 1, . . . , {b}_{n} - 1$

Thus, the new variance is

$k = \dfrac{∑ ( {a}_{i} + 1{)}^{2} + ∑ ( {b}_{i} - 1{)}^{2}}{3n} - {\left(\dfrac{\left(12n + 2n\right) + \left(3n - n\right)}{3n}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{\left(∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + 2n + 2 ∑ {a}_{i}\right) + \left(∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2} + n - 2 ∑ {b}_{i}\right)}{3n} - {\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{∑ {\left({a}_{i}\right)}^{2} + ∑ {\left({b}_{i}\right)}^{2} + 3n + 2 ∑ {a}_{i} - 2 ∑ {b}_{i}}{3n} - {\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)}^{2}$

On putting the given values and value from the equation $\left(i\right),$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{87n + 3n + 2 ( 12n ) - 2 ( 3n )}{3n} - {\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{108}{3} - {\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ 9k = 3 ( 108 ) - ( 16{)}^{2}$

$⇒ 9k = 324 - 256 = 68 .$

Consider the following frequency distribution:

Class: $0 - 6$ $6 - 12$ $12 - 18$ $18 - 24$ $24 - 30$
Frequency: $a$ $b$ $12$ $9$ $5$

If mean $= \dfrac{309}{22}$ and median $= 14,$ then the value $( a - b{)}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Class Frequency Mid-point $\left({x}_{i}\right)$ ${f}_{i}{x}_{i}$
$0 - 6$ $a$ $\dfrac{0 + 6}{2} = 3$ $3a$
$6 - 12$ $b$ $\dfrac{6 + 12}{2} = 9$ $9b$
$12 - 18$ $12$ $\dfrac{12 + 18}{2} = 15$ $180$
$18 - 24$ $9$ $\dfrac{18 + 24}{2} = 21$ $189$
$24 - 30$ $5$ $\dfrac{24 + 30}{2} = 27$ $135$
$N = \left(26 + a + b\right)$ $\left(504 + 3a + 9b\right)$

We know that, mean$= \dfrac{∑ {f}_{i}{x}_{i}}{∑ {f}_{i}}$

Given, mean$= \dfrac{309}{22}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3a + 9b + 180 + 189 + 135}{a + b + 26} = \dfrac{309}{22}$

$⇒ \dfrac{504 + 3a + 9b}{a + b + 26} = \dfrac{309}{22}$

$⇒ 66a + 198b + 11088 = 309a + 309b + 8034$

$⇒ 243a + 111b = 3054$

$⇒ 81a + 37b = 1018 . . . \left(1\right)$

Now, median$= 14,$ which lies in the interval $12 - 18,$ thus $12 - 18$ is the median class and we have $= l + \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{N}{2} - c\right) \times h}{f},$

Where, $l$ is the lower limit of the median class i.e. $l = 12, c$ is the cumulative frequency of the class above the median class i.e. $c = a + b, f$ is the frequency of the median class i.e. $f = 12$ and $h$ is the length of the interval i.e. $h = 6 .$

Thus, we have $12 + \left(\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{a + b + 26}{2}\right) - ( a + b )}{12}\right) \times 6 = 14$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{a + b + 26 - 2a - 2b}{2}\right)}{2} = 14 - 12$

$⇒ \dfrac{26 - a - b}{4} = 2$

$⇒ 26 - a - b = 8$

$⇒ a + b = 18 . . . \left(2\right)$

On solving the equations $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right),$ we get $a = 8, b = 10 .$

$∴ {\left(a - b\right)}^{2} = {\left(8 - 10\right)}^{2} = 4 .$

questions.q: The mean and variance of $7$ observations are $8$ and $16$ respectively. If one observation $14$ is omitted, $a$ and $b$ are respectively mean and variance of remaining $6$ observation, then $a + 3b - 5$ is equal to ________
questions.solution:
Given,

Mean and variance of $7$ observation is given as $8 \text{ and } 16$ respectively,

So using the formula of mean we get, $\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{S}{7} ⇒ S = 8 \times 7 = 56$

Now if we remove $14$ sum will be $S = 56 - 14 = 42$ and new mean will be $a = \dfrac{42}{6} = 7$

Now using the formula of variance we get,

$\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{6}{x}_{i}^{2} + {14}^{2}}{7} - {\left(\overset{¯}{x}\right)}^{2} = 16$

$⇒ \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{6}{x}_{i}^{2} + {14}^{2}}{7} - {8}^{2} = 16$

$⇒ \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{6}{x}_{i}^{2} + {14}^{2}}{7} = 80$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{6}{x}_{i}^{2} + {14}^{2} = 560$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{6}{x}_{i} = 364$

Now, new variance $b = \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{6}{x}_{i}^{2}}{6} - {a}^{2} = \dfrac{364}{6} - {7}^{2} = \dfrac{35}{3}$

Hence, the value of $a + 3b - 5 = 7 + 35 - 5 = 37$
